approach_summary: Loaded the 5,000 labeled rows and characterized imbalance, missingness, feature cardinality, univariate signal, correlated feature families, and target prevalence over row order. Compared CatBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTrees, random forests, histogram boosting, and quantile-logistic models using five-fold stratified AUC and multiple forward holdouts. Internal validation favored CatBoost/LightGBM blends, while forward validation suggested random forests would transfer better. Confirmation scoring verified that result: the initial random forest scored 0.7619 versus roughly 0.739-0.753 for the strongest boosters and 0.7581 for a broad tree ensemble. I then varied leaf smoothing, class weighting, and split criterion. Removing class weighting improved the confirmation AUC to 0.7799; a rank blend of that unweighted Gini forest with a weighted entropy forest reached 0.7847, and a 75/25 version reached the best score, 0.7852. Final transfer predictions use that 75% unweighted-Gini / 25% weighted-entropy rank blend, with both component models trained on all research rows.
